newsitem.title: POLAND: Foreign-charged zloty rises, Polish c.bank looks on.
newsitem.headline: Foreign-charged zloty rises, Polish c.bank looks on.

text.p: The zloty returned to the offensive on Tuesday, rising against the basket of currencies amid foreign investor entry in Polish bonds, dealers said.

They said that the Polish market, still shell-shocked from repeated National Bank of Poland currency-buying interventions last week, cautiously inched up during today's session waiting for an intervention which did not materialise.

"The zloty, likely charged by foreign entry into Polish treasuries, gradually strengthened on Tuesday as the central bank refrained from intervening," said Piotr Czyzewski of ING Bank in Warsaw. "But they could intervene at any moment now."
However, some said that money market rates could rise by as much as one percentage point as liquidity drops before the new higher deposit requirements take effect on February 28.
On Tuesday overnight rates inched up to close at 21.25/21.45 percent versus opening's 21.05/21.17 percent as cash flows tightened for end-of-month reserve squaring.
